problems.source_says: The panel comprises the researcher and two native speakers. The researcher is identified as the school's Head of Research for Educational Development in its Academic Department and is described implementing classroom teaching and assigning writing tasks. Codebook section 6 reserves human_raters for lay raters or crowd workers and includes instructors and professionals under expert_raters. Consequently, a lay-rater classification for this panel is not established: at least one scorer has a professional/instructional role, while the two native speakers' professional qualifications are unreported. Human scoring itself is confirmed; the unqualified rater-subtype code is the problem.
problems.quote: During the evaluation phase, the resulting writing tasks underwent rigorous assessment by the researcher and two native speakers.
problems.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 23), Research Instruments, item 3, Creative Writing Skills Assessment; researcher affiliation on PDF p. 1 (printed p. 17), author footnote; classroom teaching role on PDF p. 6 (printed p. 22), Research Instruments, item 2. Creativity codebook section 6, Measure, lines 93-94.

problems.source_says: The Voice criterion rates the appropriateness and quality of a single narrative's voice: it should be distinct, fitting for the narrator or speaker, and sustained throughout the narrative. This fits usefulness, which explicitly includes appropriateness or quality of a single output in codebook section 6. Coding this as the residual other construct overlooks that definition; it is not a comparison of voices across different people.
problems.quote: A notable hallmark of the student's writing prowess lies in the creation of a distinct and fitting voice for the narrator or speaker.
problems.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 24), Table 1, item 3, Voice (5 Points). Creativity codebook section 6, Construct, lines 79 and 85.

problems.source_says: The Literary Devices criterion rates the quality and appropriateness of metaphor, simile, symbolism, and personification in a single composition, emphasizing skillful, seamless integration without gimmickry or forced inclusion. Under codebook section 6, appropriateness and quality of a single output belong to usefulness. The other code therefore misclassifies this writing-quality criterion.
problems.quote: Importantly, these devices are seamlessly integrated, avoiding any semblance of gimmickry or forced inclusion, thus contributing organically to the overall composition.
problems.locator: PDF p. 8 (printed p. 24), Table 1, item 4, Literary Devices (5 Points). Creativity codebook section 6, Construct, lines 79 and 85.

summary: Criterion 3 holds: raters scored student-written narratives produced without AI after the intervention, and the reported statistics match the PDF. Coding is refuted because the lay-rater classification is unsupported and Voice and Literary Devices fit the codebook's usefulness/quality construct rather than other.
